body:
## Objective and author authorization — 2026-10-09
Adjust physical systems and derived-stat growth to a coherent metric convention. The author requests this issue, approves the new growth formulas/mapping and Earth gravity, and requires JumpZ recalibration. Current inspected baseline: 5.1.9, main f8addb685022a867dd76071826304860ea97baa9.

Goals: make early attribute investment more noticeable relative to the endpoint; curb the old very large high-level multipliers; use consistent metres, seconds, kilograms, joules and watts without resizing existing maps or characters.

## 1. Approved growth curves
Let N be the effective attribute level:
- B(N) = (N*N + 25*N)/125, expressed in percentage points.
- New Type 1: bonus B(N).
- New Type 2: bonus 3*B(N).
- New Type 3: bonus 7*B(N).
- For multiplicative growth of a nonzero base, M = 1 + bonus/100.

Author's FINAL mapping (supersedes earlier discussion):
| Old curve | New curve |
| --- | --- |
| Old Type 1: 100 + N(N+1)/2 | New Type 3 |
| Old Type 2: N(N+1)/101 | New Type 1 |
| Old Type 3: decreasing complement of old Type 2 | New Type 1, retaining the appropriate decreasing operation |
| Old Type 4: 100 + 2N(N+1)/101 | New Type 2 |

At N=0 all bonuses are zero; at N=100 bonuses are 100%, 300%, 700%, giving x2/x4/x8 when added to a 100% base. These are NOT powers of the Type 1 multiplier at intermediate levels.

Keep curve and operation separate: direct percentage, additive bonus, complement, multiplier or divisor. Preserve existing probability caps, minimum-zero remainders, base bonuses and operation order unless explicitly changed. Do not turn percentage-point damage subtraction into multiplicative damage mitigation. Preserve legitimate above-100 effective levels; 100 is the comparison reference, not a newly approved hard attribute cap.

Audit every consumer, including duplicated/inlined player/NPC formulas, equipment bonuses, Tarot/Trucazo, dialogue, Box integer capacity, resource maxima/regeneration/costs, survival, criticals, evasion, Pain/Lucidity/health penalties, movement, Toughness mitigation and thermal thresholds/acclimatization. Actual current rules take precedence over legacy unused fields. In particular, ordinary Toughness subtraction, thermal damage resistance and threshold widening have different operations despite sharing the old Type 2 curve.

Reference values for B: N=1 -> 0.208%; 10 -> 2.8%; 25 -> 10%; 50 -> 30%; 75 -> 60%; 100 -> 100%.

## 2. Approved spatial/time convention and gravity
- Retain 32 map units (MU) = 1 metre.
- Retain 35 simulation tics = 1 real simulation second.
- Do not change TICRATE or rescale world geometry, bodies, sprites or distances.
- Distance: metres = MU/32.
- Velocity: m/s = (MU/tic)*35/32; engine velocity = (m/s)*32/35.
- Acceleration: m/s^2 = (MU/tic^2)*35^2/32.
- Earth gravity: 9.81 m/s^2 -> 9.81*32/1225 = 0.25626122449 MU/tic^2.
- This number is the desired effective acceleration in ordinary conditions, NOT a value to copy blindly into every engine gravity setting. Verify GZDoom 4.14.2 global/sector/actor semantics and avoid applying the factor twice.
- Keep intentional no-gravity/flying states and local gravity modifiers coherent.
- Keep accelerated world-calendar time separate from mechanical simulation time.

Centralize unit conversions and physical data; audit hardcoded native/SI mixtures in movement, impacts, traps, ranged weapons, NPCs and heat. Preserve explicitly approved physical quantities (e.g. cannon muzzle speed) when converting; do not reinterpret an engine Speed number as metres per second.

## 3. Approved movement, attack cycle and energy-based jump — author follow-up 2026-10-09

### Attack and movement
- Attack speed and movement speed use NEW Type 2: M2(N)=1+3*(N*N+25*N)/12500, x4 at 100.
- Physical attack speed uses Dexterity; retain the existing base cycle (14 tics), weapon/glove weight versus carrying-capacity penalty, thermal modifiers, and attack-impact/recovery fractions. Faster attacks shorten the existing full cycle, not an additional duplicate recovery. Preserve distinct ammunition reload/cast/skill cooldown routes.
- Author-confirmed base steady forward speeds at Agility 0 without penalties: walking 4 m/s (128 MU/s, 3.657142857 MU/tic), running 8 m/s (256 MU/s, 7.314285714 MU/tic). Retain the 2:1 run/walk ratio. Both scale with M2(Agility): at 100, walking 16 m/s and running 32 m/s. Apply existing relevant status/load modifiers separately. Calibrate native movement input/friction to measured travel speed rather than assigning these velocity numbers directly to ForwardMove multipliers.
- The currently implemented acceleration envelope is f_next=f+(1-f)*0.028127624 per tic, reaching 95% of the input multiplier after 3 seconds of continuous input; actual velocity also depends on native physics. No replacement acceleration model has yet been approved. Preserve that envelope pending an explicit replacement decision; the 800 W / 3 s calculation motivated the chosen speed but is not a new constant-power controller.
- The author is exploring force/power/mass-based acceleration. Constant acceleration gives v=v0+a*t; constant net acceleration power gives v^2=v0^2+2*P*t/m. These are different assumptions. Power alone does not define a finite top speed without losses or a speed target. A target-speed plus force/power-limited acceleration model is a proposal, not a finalized numeric contract.

### Approved jump contract
Let mb be biological body mass in kg, mt be total moved mass (body plus carried load), and A be effective Agility:
- E0 = 800*(mb/80)^0.75 joules.
- E_jump = E0*M3(A), with M3(A)=1+7*(A*A+25*A)/12500.
- v0 = sqrt(2*E_jump/mt) m/s.
- JumpZ = v0*32/35 MU/tic.
- Ideal rise h = E_jump/(mt*g), using actual local effective gravity.
- 800 J is the approved 80 kg reference: 800 W of useful mechanical output integrated for one second. This is an energy reference, not a newly required one-second jump wind-up. Do not apply muscular efficiency to this useful energy a second time.
- At 80 kg, no load/status penalties: A=0 -> 800 J, JumpZ=4.088810, ideal rise=1.019368 m; A=100 -> 6400 J, JumpZ=11.564901, ideal rise=8.154944 m under Earth gravity.
- Use total mass in kinetic energy; replace the old independent load multiplier on JumpZ to avoid charging the same load twice. Preserve relevant air/survival/health/elemental and immobilization behavior, and document how these modifiers change actual delivered energy.
- Verify discrete native apex/airtime against continuous references.
- Replace the old fixed 0.5 m jump thermal-work budget with the new delivered jump energy, charged once per accepted jump. No additional Air/Hunger debit is inferred from joules.

### Falls and preserved mass behavior
The author approves proportional fall-threshold rescaling for the new gravity, not unrelated collision redesign:
- For unchanged reference drop heights, velocity thresholds scale by sqrt(g_new/g_old); squared-speed or energy-per-mass thresholds scale by g_new/g_old.
- For the old ordinary 1 MU/tic^2 baseline: g_old=38.28125 m/s^2; g_new/g_old=0.25626122449; velocity factor approximately 0.506223.
- Audit the existing jump-related biological landing absorption and apply the new jump contract consistently. Do not multiply every threshold by the same factor or apply both recalculated gravity and a duplicate correction.
- Preserve existing mass dependencies of maximum health/regeneration, carrying capacity/derivatives, effort Air consumption/derivatives, passive Hunger/Thirst and their recovery, resistance to being pushed, collisions and falls. “Preserve” means the actual existing equations, including nonlinear knockback/collision relations, not rewriting them all as linear.
- Keep real total mass in momentum, kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy; biological mass remains the thermal-inertia input.

## 4. Approved precision, damage, push, launch and projectile policy

### Weapon output and dispersion
- Physical and magical accuracy use NEW Type 3.
- Seven dispersion categories become min=k degrees, max=10*k degrees, for k=1..7: 1–10, 2–20, 3–30, 4–40, 5–50, 6–60, 7–70 degrees.
- These are dispersion categories, distinct from equipment quality tiers. Preserve category assignments and existing precision operation, sampling and aiming modifiers.
- Keep weapon base damage and existing damage, push and launch equations; replace their old growth with NEW Type 3. The author's latest instruction supersedes earlier exploratory replacement of melee/push equations with universal force/power equations or new mass exponents.
- Previously discussed athletic references (80 kg, 1000 N and 800 W; force exponent 2/3 and power exponent 0.75, without sex/race coefficients) are design context, not authorization to overwrite the preserved combat formulas. The 800 J jump reference and its mass exponent ARE explicitly approved above.
- Do not conflate mechanical watts/joules with existing gameplay damage or magic units.

### Projectile gravity and NPC aiming
- All ranged-weapon projectiles except elemental projectiles are to be affected by gravity. Preserve deliberately authored elemental/seeking behavior.
- NPCs using nonmagical projectiles should compensate drop with a ballistic trajectory if implementation/performance cost is modest. Compute at launch rather than solving every projectile every tic; preserve dispersion, do not silently add perfect aim or target-motion prediction.
- If the ballistic extension is materially costly, report that limitation rather than inventing another author policy.
- Inventory launch speeds, gravity and aiming for arrows, bolts, bullets, pellets, javelins and cannons. No unapproved muzzle speeds or drag model.

Verified baseline:
- Carbine Projectile flags include NOGRAVITY; arrows, bolts and pellets inherit gravity-free flight.
- Javelins explicitly clear NOGRAVITY.
- Cannon FastProjectile manually subtracts GetGravity once per physical tic; preserve single integration (KNOWN_PITFALLS CA-KP-014).
- Soldier aiming currently targets the current centre with dispersion and no drop compensation.
- Cannon targeting currently approximates vertical compensation as g*t*(t+1)/2. Revalidate with actual projectile gravity.
- Validate shots at different ranges/elevations, unreachable-target handling and trajectory/collision consistency.

## 5. Muscular efficiency and thermal work

### Approved efficiency
The author approved averaging Agility and Dexterity, then applying NEW Type 1:
- N_eff = (Agility + Dexterity)/2.
- eta_raw = 0.25*M1(N_eff), with M1(N)=1+(N*N+25*N)/12500.
- Thus both attributes at 0 -> 25%; both at 100 -> 50%.
- Average attributes BEFORE evaluating the nonlinear curve; do not average the two curve outputs.
- Author follow-up: muscular efficiency is capped at 99%: eta=min(0.99, eta_raw). Preserve effective attribute levels above 100; this caps efficiency only, not attributes. Never allow negative muscular heat.

### Reuse existing action budgets
The current #136/#140 ledger already defines mechanical work separately from Air:
- Walking/running: 0.5025/1.005 J per kg of moved mass per metre; positive ascent adds m*g*h once.
- Weapon-specific fixed joule budgets; charged x2 and sweeps x3 once each; natural attacks and firearms have dedicated profiles.
- Active swimming has sustained effort profiles.
- Pushing/blocking have isometric profiles, and descent has a braking profile.
These budgets do not all need to be invented again. Preserve them except for the explicitly replaced jump budget and necessary gravity/unit consistency.

For positive mechanical work W:
- E_metabolic = W/eta.
- Q_muscular = W*(1/eta - 1).
- With a fixed metabolic budget, W=eta*E_metabolic and Q=(1-eta)*E_metabolic.
Use one consistent budget boundary: do not independently fix both W and E_metabolic while changing eta. Existing action costs specify work; higher efficiency reduces the metabolic cost/heat of that same work. At fixed metabolic energy, efficiency can instead increase useful output. Do not apply an additional unapproved speed multiplier on top of the approved Type-2 speeds.
- Faster completion alone does not change fixed action work, but more actions per second increase heat per second.
- Isometric effort must retain a separate metabolic cost at zero external work; do not replace it with W=0 -> no heat.
- Negative work must not become cooling.
- Basal heat, shivering, sweat, breathing and environmental/magical exchange stay separate.
- Do not infer new Hunger/Air resource charges from the thermal energy ledger.
- Do not restore the removed post-effort heat tail or conflate real simulation seconds with world-calendar seconds.

Carry forward #152 / PR #153 and #130/#140/#136 findings. Validate thermal energy against actual accepted actions, gravity, mass, efficiency and action frequency. Higher maximum statistics must not automatically count as continuously exerted maximum power.

## 6. Remaining author parameters before dependent implementation
- Any replacement of the existing acceleration envelope by a force/power-based model remains a separate author decision; approved 4/8 m/s baselines can be implemented with the retained envelope.
- Explicit handling of any material-cost limitation in NPC ballistic aiming.

All other decisions above are authorized design requirements. Do not substitute exploratory numbers for these remaining choices. Updating this issue does not claim game-code implementation.

## Acceptance and delivery
- [ ] Every old growth consumer mapped to the new family with its correct operation; shared player/NPC results and UI agree.
- [ ] Curve fixtures cover 0/1/10/25/50/75/100 and effective levels above 100; validate caps, complements, divisors and integer capacity.
- [ ] Effective ordinary gravity is 9.81 m/s^2 under 32 MU/m and 35 tics/s, with no calendar or double-gravity scaling.
- [ ] Author-selected SI movement/jump targets are documented and measured natively; load/status effects remain coherent.
- [ ] Projectile inventory, straight/ballistic/seek distinctions and NPC/cannon aiming are verified at multiple distances/elevations.
- [ ] Falls, impacts, vertical impulses, traps, effort heat and critical map traversals have focused regression evidence.
- [ ] Dispersion categories 1–7 and new Type-3 precision agree across player/NPC/UI.
- [ ] Jump fixtures cover biological versus carried mass and new Type-3 energy; thermal work is charged once.
- [ ] Efficiency averaging, positive-work heat and separate isometric/braking budgets are verified; the approved 99% efficiency cap holds above level 100.
- [ ] Existing saves retain attributes, ownership and persistent gameplay state; derived values recalculate through explicit idempotent migration where needed. Document resource/maxima migration and test protected old-save copies and rollback.
- [ ] Update consolidated SYSTEMS/PROJECT/TASKS/HISTORY/CONTEXT/README and index as applicable; preserve historical formulas as history, not live contracts.
- [ ] One focused branch and linked PR, with separable curve/physics changes. Follow AGENTS.md and GZDOOM_DEVELOPMENT; static/native results and outstanding author acceptance remain distinct. No implementation, release assignment or merge is claimed by issue creation.


## Implementation clarification approved by the author ? 2026-10-09
On the first load with the new curves, preserve the percentages of Health, Anima, Air and Adrenaline. Health rounds to a native integer while keeping a living character alive. Scale underwater Air-recovery debt with its maximum as well. This is a versioned, idempotent migration; ordinary equipment recalculation keeps its existing clamp/no-free-heal behavior. Keep protected original saves and the matching previous package for rollback.
title: [V5 / Physics & Statistics] Align physical systems with SI units and replace attribute growth curves
